nodes.question: What autonomous region of Portugal comprises Madeira and Porto Santo?
nodes.answer: The Madeira Archipelago is the autonomous region that comprises Madeira and Porto Santo.
nodes.paragraph: 2021; Vilizzi et al. 2021).Laying in the north Atlantic, the Madeira Archi- pelago is an autonomous region of Portugal that comprises Madeira and Porto Santo, the two main populated islands of the archipelago, as well as the Desertas Islands and the Selvagens Islands. Over the past two decades, there has been a growing research interest in marine bioinvasions in the region, primar - ily due to the establishment of a dedicated research group. nodes.question: What is the focus of the paper related to fish stocks?
nodes.answer: The paper focuses on transboundary fish stocks that distribute across two or more exclusive economic zones (EEZs) due to adult movement or larval dispersal.
nodes.paragraph: 2023). Yet practical challenges exist for marine reserves to be successfully implemented. Many species move over large distances as adults or lar - vae, which can be at odds with the spatial boundaries of a reserve (Cowen and Sponaugle 2009 ; Song et al. 2017 ). Furthermore, reserves that produce measurable outcomes require sustainable financing to support staffing and enforce- ment, which can be challenging for low-capacity countries (Grorud-Colvert et al. 2021; Millage et al. 2021). nodes.question: In which provinces of China have the ETS pilots been launched since 2013?
nodes.answer: The ETS pilots have been launched in Shenzhen, Shanghai, Beijing, Guangdong, Tianjin, Hubei, Chongqing, and Fujian provinces.
nodes.paragraph: Since 2013, China S ETS pilots have been launched successively in Shenzhen, Shanghai, Beijing, Guangdong, Tianjin, Hubei, Chongqing and Fujian provinces. These pilots have covered nearly 3000 key emissions enterprises with a cumulative trading volume of 455 million tons, and a turnover of 10.55 billion yuan (approximately) till December 2020. The booming development of eight pilots thus promote the realization of carbon peak by 2030 and carbon neutral by 2060 in China (Liu & Sun, 2021 ;Q ie ta I , 2021 ; Xiao et al., 2021 ). However, the carbon price as a signal that transmits information in carbon markets, uc- tuates violently due to a large number of potential factors such as macroeconomic events (Duc et al., 2021 ;K o C he ta I , 2014 ), energy prices (Adekoya, 2021 ; Balcilar et al., 2016 ), politically-driven policies (Duan et al., 2018 ), and overall situation of industry development from the macro and long-term perspectives as well as the supply and demand of carbon assets from the micro and short-term perspectives.
